To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a method that can learn new capabilities in a deep neural network without hindering performance on the original tasks, and with a substantially reduced number of additional parameters.

(i) DANs learn new capabilities while preserving performance on the original tasks, (ii) they do so with a small number of parameters (typically around 13% of the original), and (iii) they can be quantized to 3% of their original size while incurring negligible or no loss of accuracy.

we propose an approach that learns new tasks with minimal parameter overhead, preserves the original network’s performance on the original tasks, and can switch between multiple learned representations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of incremental learning through deep adaptation.
the problem of how to incrementally learn new tasks with a neural network without losing previously learned capabilities.
the question of how to learn new capabilities in a neural network while maintaining the performance on existing tasks.

DANs are a very efficient and effective way to learn new capabilities in an existing neural network.
DAN is a novel and effective method for incremental learning of deep networks.

we propose a new method for incremental learning of deep convolutional networks that is more efficient in terms of the number of training cycles, the amount of memory and the number of parameters required to solve a new task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DANs are able to achieve a significant reduction in the parameter count, while maintaining or even improving the accuracy, compared to the standard fine tuning method, and are also able to achieve a better accuracy than the state of the art methods, such as joint training, with the same parameter count as the standard fine tuning methods.
we propose a novel approach to learn new tasks in neural networks without the need to retrain from scratch or incur a large increase in the number of network parameters.
our method is a powerful, parameter efficient, and scalable approach to learn new capabilities from existing trained neural networks.

a small number of linear combinations of the existing network filters are sufficient for learning a new task, while the original network filters remain unchanged.
a network can be adapted to new domains with a small number of parameters by learning linear combinations of its existing filters.
it is possible to learn new tasks in a way that is more efficient and more effective than standard fine-tuning methods.
